newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oil tanker arrives at Iraq's Mina al-Bakr - paper.
newsitem.headline: Oil tanker arrives at Iraq's Mina al-Bakr - paper.

text.p: An oil tanker docked at Iraq's Mina al-Bakr export terminal in the northern Gulf on Saturday to load the first cargo of oil from the terminal in six years, the United Arab Emirates paper Khaleej Times reported on Sunday.
The Bahamas-flagged 274,585-tonne MT Star Africa arrived at Mina al-Bakr from Dubai and was being guided into the terminal last night, Khaleej Times reported.
The tanker's charterer and destination of the vessel was unknown.

Under an oil-for-food deal agreed with the United Nations, Iraq will export between 500,000 and 600,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude at current prices from the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan and al-Bakr.
Al-Bakr, 12 miles (19 km) off the southern Fao Peninsula, allows Iraq to export its oil to lucrative Asian markets.
U.S. oil firm Coastal Corp sought to fix an Ultra Large Crude Carrier (ULCC) to load crude at al-Bakr in September for its refinery in the Caribbean island of Aruba.
A tanker also arrived at Ceyhan on Saturday.
